interest: Shows U.S. resistance to Allied objections regarding vessel armaments, preserving SCAP's authority to establish Japan's coastal patrol.
overview: This file documents U.S. State Department policy formulation and diplomatic negotiations in April and May 1948 concerning the Japanese Maritime Safety Authorities Bill (Law No. 35). It details American efforts to resist Far Eastern Commission intervention and Allied objections over vessel size and armaments, defending SCAP's independent authority to create a Japanese coastal patrol against smuggling and illegal immigration.
